<reason>Side A overcame a proposition phrased favorably for PRO by exposing a fatal dilemma in Side B's case regarding labor scarcity and nighttime safety. While Side B relied on eloquent appeals to autonomy and the qualifier "when possible," Side A demonstrated that a finite caregiver workforce cannot supply one-on-one overnight care across scattered private homes without starving collective facilities of staff, and that waiting for strict "medical necessity" traps mobility-impaired elders in isolated houses until a crisis occurs.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>In Turn 8 [A4.1, A4.3], Side A dismantled Side B's defense by catching a direct contradiction: Side B dismissed 24/7 home staffing as a "strawman" in favor of part-time care during Pressure Questions [B3.1] to dodge labor-scarcity critiques, but immediately pivoted to promising "overnight aides" and "24/7 support" in Rebuttal 2 [B4.1, B4.4] to answer who helps a frail elder at 2:00 a.m.</best_rebuttal>
